title: DenseOpenBaseChangeComparison
statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field and P=(X,A) a curve coefficient pair [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting] with constructible torsion abelian sheaf A [def-weil-pbc-constructible-torsion]. Let U be a dense open of X, j its inclusion, and B=j_!j^*A [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. Use the coefficient equivalence E from abelian groups to modules over ULift Z, defined by the inverse of the forgetful equivalence from Z-modules followed by restriction of scalars along ULift Z ≃ Z. Put F=E(A) and G=E(B). Write T(F) for the alternative that F has invertible-order torsion or is p-primary for a prime p=char(k) [def-weil-pbc-primary-torsion]. C6(G) implies C6(F), and C7(G) implies C7(F). Under T(F) the reverse implications hold as well. Here C6 and C7 are conditional invertible-order and proper base-change assertions [def-weil-pbc-C6], [def-weil-pbc-C7].

proof.text: The inverse Z-module equivalence followed by restriction along ULift Z ≃ Z gives the coefficient functor E. Restrict its adjunction with its inverse to sheaf categories using fully faithful sheaf-to-presheaf functors. Open restriction commutes definitionally with postcomposition. Uniqueness of left adjoints identifies E(j_!j^*A) with j_!j^*E(A); compose with upperStarIsoOpenImmersionRestriction on both sides. This is the fully proved private dense_open_coefficient_iso, with no cohomological assumptions.

Reuse the existing fully proved private AlgebraicGeometry.IsCurve.dense_open_all_base_change from DenseOpenBaseChange through proof-only import all. Its proof combines the low-degree comparison with the original and pulled-back higher-degree counit bijections in a naturality square, splitting q ≤ 1 versus 1 < q. This yields all-degree comparison equivalence for module coefficients without introducing another helper or obligation.

An isomorphism of coefficient sheaves induces bijections on cohomology on X and after inverse image. Apply the same naturality square to the coefficient isomorphism from step 1 to obtain the all-degree comparison equivalence between the actual F and G of the statement.

The counit j_!j^*F → F is monic by the open-closed short exact sequence. Compose it with the coefficient isomorphism to obtain a monomorphism G → F. Its geometric-stalk maps are injective, so primary torsion and invertible-order torsion pass from F to G. If G is p-primary and has invertible-order torsion in characteristic p, each stalk element is annihilated by p^b and by an integer n invertible in k. The prime p cannot divide n, hence these integers are coprime; Bezout gives that the element is zero. Geometric stalk conservativity gives G zero. Forgetting coefficients and inverse image preserve zero, and the proved cohomology lemma Sheaf.subsingleton_H_of_isZero makes every comparison for G bijective.

For C6(G) → C6(F), introduce the invertible-order hypothesis on F and use its transfer to G before applying the all-degree equivalence. For the reverse implication, split the given torsion alternative: use C6(F) in the invertible-order case, and the zero-sheaf argument in the primary case. For C7 in either direction, introduce properness and apply the same all-degree equivalence; its reverse implication does not need the supplied torsion alternative. Pair the four implications without altering the statement.
